text:
maya: Heads-up — starting 2025-04-07 we'll require signed SDK releases and start publishing code-sample provenance metadata in the docs. This affects the hosted Py/JS wheels and the code snippets we ship in docs. :loudspeaker:
kenji: Is there an RFC or writeup we can review?
maya: RFC draft is linked in the internal RFCs page: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/sdk-signing (please comment)
olivia-k: For Private installs, does this mean customers need to trust a Redwood key locally?
maya: Yes — Private customers will need to import our verification key into their trust store. We'll provide an automated script and clear docs.
security-bot: Note: this change reduces supply-chain risk. Security will run a baseline SBOM + signature scan on all released artifacts.
jason: Timeline check — when do we flip enforcement?
maya: Plan: 2025-04-07 — unsigned wheel acceptance disabled by default; 2025-05-31 — signature verification enforced for installs. 60-day grace for pinned CI flows.
kenji: How will developer workflows change for local dev and CI?
maya: New helper CLI: 
```
pip download redwood-sdk==4.2.0 -d /tmp/dist
redwood-sig verify /tmp/dist/redwood_sdk-4.2.0-py3.whl --public-key ~/.redwood/pub.pem
pip install /tmp/dist/redwood_sdk-4.2.0-py3.whl
```
CI option: set REDWOOD_ALLOW_UNSIGNED=1 to preserve short-term workflows (will emit deprecation warnings in logs).
olivia-k: Will this affect our hosted SDK distribution (CDN caching etc)?
maya: No change to CDN; signed artifacts will be uploaded to the same buckets and mirrored. Docs pages will include a small "Provenance" header with an SBOM link and signature fingerprint for each sample.
jason: Anything we need from Support/Customer Success?
maya: Yes — CS will get a KB draft to share with enterprise customers, and we'll coordinate a customer notice 2 weeks before enforcement.
kenji: :thumbsup:
maya: I'll drop the RFC link in #docs once it's ready and follow up with a short internal blog. Ping me if you want to review the customer-facing wording before we post. Thanks!
